item.title: About 8,300 customers still without power in Quebec after ice storm
item.description: MONTREAL — Quebec's hydro utility was working to re-establish power for tens of thousands of customers on Thursday after an ice storm descended over the province's south, knocking down branches and turning streets and sidewalks into skating rinks.

item.title: Statistics Canada set to report jobs, unemployment data for February
item.description: OTTAWA — Statistics Canada is set to release fresh jobs data for February this morning. A Reuters poll of economists expects the economy added 10,000 jobs last month but that the unemployment rate edged up to 6.6 per cent.

item.title: Price shocks from Iran war could give Canada leverage in CUSMA talks: experts
item.description: WASHINGTON — Countries around the world are grappling with skyrocketing costs for key commodities like oil and fertilizer as the war with Iran continues to upend global trade.

item.title: Carney to observe NATO drills in northern Norway with Norwegian and German leaders
item.description: OTTAWA — Prime Minister Mark Carney is in Norway today, where he will observe NATO’s Cold Response exercises alongside the Norwegian prime minister.

item.title: Canadians turning to March break alternatives amid tensions in Cuba, Mexico
item.description: TORONTO — Many Canadian travellers have opted for alternative March break destinations this year, travel agents say, as unrest and violence disrupt tourism in some of the traditionally popular affordable destinations.

item.title: B.C. appointed them to map old-growth. Now they say province is failing to save it
item.description: Every member of a former panel the British Columbia government appointed to identify old-growth for potential protection in 2021 now says they're concerned about continued logging in those same rare and "irreplaceable" forests.
